'''''Zoboomafoo''''' is a live-action/animated [[children's television series]] that originally aired on [[PBS]] from January 25, 1999, to November 21, 2001. After the original run on public television, reruns were shown on [[Universal Kids#As PBS Kids Sprout/Sprout (2005–17)|PBS Kids Sprout]] until 2012. A total of 65 episodes were aired. A creation of the [[Kratt brothers|Kratt Brothers]] ([[Chris Kratt|Chris]] and [[Martin Kratt]]), it features an [[anthropomorphic]] [[Coquerel's sifaka]] [[lemur]] named Zoboomafoo, performed by Canadian puppeteer Gord Robertson, and mainly portrayed by a [[lemur]] named [[Jovian (lemur)|Jovian]], along with a collection of returned animal guests.<ref>{{cite web |last=Zarley |first=B. David |title=26 Years Ago, One Underrated Nature Show Drove Kids Wild |url=https://www.fatherly.com/entertainment/zoboomafoo-retrospective-wild-kratts |website=Fatherly |access-date=17 September 2026 |quote=Puppet lemur voiced and performed by Gord Robertson}}</ref>

==Production==
''Zoboomafoo'' was produced by [[PBS Kids]], [[CINAR Corporation]] (now folded into [[WildBrain]]), and the Kratt brothers' Earth Creatures company.<ref name=books>{{cite web |url=https://www.pbs.org/about/about-pbs/blogs/news/pbs-and-simon-schuster-childrens-publishing-to-launch-pbs-kids-books-february-10-2000/ |title=PBS and Simon & Schuster Children's Publishing To Launch PBS Kids Books |author=PBS Publicity |website=PBS |date=February 10, 2000 |access-date=May 26, 2020 |archive-date=May 26, 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200526230010/https://www.pbs.org/about/blogs/news/pbs-and-simon-schuster-childrens-publishing-to-launch-pbs-kids-books-february-10-2000/ |url-status=live }}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.bloomberg.com/press-releases/1999-04-13/cinar-pbs-and-the-kratt-brothers-become-partners-on |title=CINAR, PBS and the Kratt Brothers Become Partners on |website=Bloomberg |date=April 13, 1999 |access-date=May 26, 2020}}<!--Note: the title is incomplete on original webpage--></ref> Paragon Entertainment Corporation, who previously worked on ''[[Kratts' Creatures]]'', was slated to be involved with ''Zoboomafoo'' before being replaced by CINAR.<ref>[https://cocatalog.loc.gov/ US Copyright Office] Document No. V3455D786 / 2000-06-19</ref>

Partial filming for the series took place on location at the [[Duke Lemur Center]] in [[Durham, North Carolina]].<ref>{{Cite web|date=2014-11-11|title=Remembering a star: Jovian, lemur host of Zoboomafoo, passes away|url=https://lemur.duke.edu/remembering-a-star-jovian-lemur-host-of-zoboomafoo-passes-away/|access-date=2020-07-31|website=Duke Lemur Center|language=en|archive-date=November 12, 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201112042350/https://lemur.duke.edu/remembering-a-star-jovian-lemur-host-of-zoboomafoo-passes-away/|url-status=live}}</ref> The claymation segments were filmed at a studio in [[Etobicoke]], Ontario, Canada. Although the last new episode aired on PBS Kids in November 2001, many PBS stations continued to rerun ''Zoboomafoo'' episodes in syndication through 2009. Select stations aired reruns as late as 2017. In addition, Sprout aired reruns until February 2012.{{Citation needed|date=July 2020}} The show was broadcast in the United States, Canada, Latin America, Brazil, Australia, New Zealand, Europe, Middle East, and India.

After the series ended, in 2003, the Kratt Brothers began another series titled ''[[Be the Creature]]'' on the [[National Geographic (American TV channel)|National Geographic Channel]]. In 2011, they created the animated series ''[[Wild Kratts]]'', which currently airs on PBS Kids and [[TVO]]ntario.

Jovian (a captive [[Coquerel's sifaka]] housed at the [[Duke Lemur Center]]) portrayed Zoboomafoo in the live-action segments (with his parents Nigel and Flavia sometimes serving as stand-ins). On November 10, 2014, he died of [[kidney failure]] at his home at the age of 20.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://lemur.duke.edu/remembering-a-star-jovian-lemur-host-of-zoboomafoo-passes/|title=Remembering a Star: Jovan, Lemur Host of Zobomoofaoo Passes|work=[[Duke Lemur Center]]|date=2014|access-date=June 16, 2017|archive-date=November 14, 2014|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20141114000743/http://lemur.duke.edu/remembering-a-star-jovian-lemur-host-of-zoboomafoo-passes/|url-status=live}}</ref>

==Awards and nominations==
''Zoboomafoo'' received the 2001 Emmy for Outstanding Directing in a Children's Series<ref>{{cite news|last=Williams|first=Donna|title=PBS Wins Two More Daytime Emmys at Televised Ceremony|url=https://www.pbs.org/about/about-pbs/blogs/news/pbs-wins-two-more-daytime-emmys-at-televised-ceremony-may-21-2001/|access-date=April 17, 2013|newspaper=PBS News Archive|date=May 21, 2001|location=New York, NY|archive-date=February 14, 2015|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150214174029/https://www.pbs.org/aboutpbs/news/20010521_emmy.html|url-status=live}}</ref> and a [[Parents' Choice Award]] for Spring 2001 and Silver Honor for Fall 2001.<ref>{{cite web|last=Fries|first=Laura|title=Zoboomafoo|url=http://www.parents-choice.org/product.cfm?product_id=2866|work=Parents' Choice Awards: Television|publisher=Parents' Choice|access-date=April 17, 2013|archive-date=February 4, 2015|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150204121143/http://www.parents-choice.org/product.cfm?product_id=2866|url-status=dead}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|title=Zoboomafoo|url=http://www.parents-choice.org/product.cfm?product_id=5437|work=Parents' Choice Awards: Television|publisher=Parents' Choice|access-date=April 17, 2013|archive-date=February 14, 2015|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150214173758/http://www.parents-choice.org/product.cfm?product_id=5437|url-status=dead}}</ref>
==Other media==
There are also several video games for the PC based on ''Zoboomafoo'', where children learn the alphabet and animals that correlate to each letter. Some of the letters have interactive games to go with them, such as a coloring page.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.oldgamesfinder.com/?m=1&q=Zoboomafoo|title=Old Games Finder|website=Old Games Finder|access-date=June 16, 2017|archive-date=November 7, 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171107015840/http://www.oldgamesfinder.com/?m=1&q=Zoboomafoo|url-status=live}}</ref>
